description:
The Indian Health Service (IHS) is conducting a SOURCES SOUGHT/REQUEST FOR INFORMATION for Planning Purposes as outlined in FAR 5.101(c) to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of firms especially small businesses including: Native American/Indian-Owned Businesses (Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE)), 8(a) Certified Small Businesses, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUB-Zone) Small Businesses, Women Owned Small Businesses, Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), Small Disadvantaged Businesses (SDB), and Veteran Owned Small Businesses. 

 NO PROPOSALS ARE BEING REQUESTED OR ACCEPTED WITH THIS RFI. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this notice. Respondents will NOT be notified of the results of this notice. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this notice or any follow-up information requested. 

 Market research is being performed pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to identify businesses capable of performing the functions described herein and to support acquisition planning. 

 SUMMARY OF SCOPE 

 This project will replace the existing filtration system of the Dry Creek water treatment plant (WTP) serving the community of Warm Springs, OR. The existing filtration system has several deficiencies that are affecting the performance and increasing the difficulty of operating and maintaining the WTP. The replacement filtration system will consist of one or more containerized filtration units that utilize ceramic membrane filtration. The contractor shall furnish and install the filtration unit(s) into the existing WTP processes to provide safe drinking water for the community. 

 The filtration system is a Greenleaf design (developed by Degremont). There are several deficiencies in the filtration system, including out of spec filter media, a lack of isolation and drain valves, and inadequate backwashing. Additionally, a recent camera inspection of the underdrains identified cracking along the length of one of the cells under drain piping. 

 The filtration unit(s) will have to be compatible with and connected to several of the existing WTPs systems. These include the piping system (e.g. Raw Water, Washwater disposal, etc.), the electrical system, the control system, and the chemical treatment system. Additionally, the replacement filtration system will be subject to EPA Region 10 review. EPA’s requirements are described in the SOW, and coordination with the EPA during the review process will be required as part of the contract. 

 The designer will need to be capable of advanced water treatment process design, as well as building design (e.g. architectural, structural, etc.). The performance of the replacement filtration system shall be able to meet the EPA Primary Drinking water standards. 

 During the construction phase, capability requirements include the cooperation of the designer and builder, including project management and superintendence required of a typical general contractor, all of the applicable subcontractors for building, and site work, and in addition the full suite of engineering services needed. The contractor will be responsible for providing housing possibilities and per diem for their workers who are not local, and maintaining a constant presence on site. Performance requirements of the construction will be developed as part of the 100% technical specifications, and will be verified during the filtration system commissioning. 

 The design shall be completed in accordance with the 2025 A/E Design Guide. 

 The anticipated project magnitude is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. 

 The contract is anticipated to commence in late spring of 2027 with an approximate performance period of 600 calendar days after receipt of Notice to Proceed. TERO is applicable. 

 The type of work to be performed will be categorized under PSC code Z2NE, Repair Or Alteration Of Water Supply Facilities and NAICS code 237110 Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction with a size standard of $45 million. 

 The proposed project is anticipated to be procured as a competitive, firm-fixed-price, two-phase design-build contract in accordance with FAR Part 15 and FAR 36.101-2, using a best-value tradeoff process. Following evaluation of Phase I proposals, only the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to submit Phase II proposals. 

 PROSPECTIVE OFFEROR CAPABILITY RESPONSES - SUBMITTAL 

 Responses to this notice must be emailed to Matt Sanders at matt.sanders@ihs.gov and must be received no later than 2:00 pm PT, 9 Dec 2026. Prospective offeror capability responses must include all items below: 

 Company Information: Company name, website, physical address, SAM UEI code 

 Point of Contact: Contact name, phone number, and E-mail address 

 If a solicitation is issued, will your firm/company be submitting a proposal? Indicate Yes or No 

 Type of Business: Native American-owned (IEE/ISBEE), SBA certified 8(a), SBA Certified HUB Zone, Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), Women Owned Small Business (WOSB), and/or Small Businesses (SB). 	 Completed Attachment 1: IHS IEE Representation Form (Jan 2022) 
	 The controlling enterprise’s Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs Certificate of Degree of Indian Blood documentation.
